corrections.comment: 7727-37-9 is dinitrogen -- N2, the inert gas that is 78% of the air. `Nitrogen, organic bound` is not a compound: it is the nitrogen locked inside the organic matter of a discharge, reported as a mass of nitrogen, and no registry number can name it because a number names one compound and this is a measurement over many. BAFU writes the gas's number on all four of its organic-bound rows -- water groundwater long-term, ocean, river and unspecified -- exactly as ecoinvent does on its five and EF 3.1 on its five, so the number has to come off here too or the merge is handed lists that disagree about whether a nutrient load is nitrogen gas (#26). Removed rather than corrected: there is nothing to correct it to, and with it gone the rows group by name onto the same flow object the other lists' do. BAFU's own `Nitrogen` rows keep the number, which is theirs. The reasoning and the evidence are in ef-3.1-manual-fixes.json. (#57, #4)

corrections.comment: BAFU writes the unit into the name of ten of its flows, and the general rule takes it back off wherever the tail is the row's own unit (#67). It declines this one, correctly: the name says `m3` and the unit field says `Nm3`, and a normal cubic metre is gas measured at a stated temperature and pressure rather than a volume, so the two do not agree about what was measured. Which of them to believe is not something a pattern can decide, and it is decided here: the unit field is believed, because the name is the field this list does not keep the measure in. EF 3.1 already holds `Gas, Mine, Off-gas, Process, Coal Mining` in `resources / in ground`, which is where this row belongs; with the suffix gone it reaches that flow instead of minting a second one beside it, and the normal cubic metre survives as its unit. (#67, #4)

The other `Nm3` row, same disagreement between the name and the unit field, same reading of it. Both of BAFU's are natural gas measured in normal cubic metres. Unlike the row above this one does not then match: it carries CAS 8006-14-2, and two flow objects in the list answer to `Gas, natural` -- natural gas itself and the coal-mine off-gas, which has natural gas's CAS synonyms hanging off the same number -- so it is reported as `multiple-flow-object-candidates` rather than placed. Fixing the name here is still right and is separable: it is what the vendor's row means, and it stops the row being unmatched for two reasons at once. (#67, #4)

The unit is out of the name for the same reason it is out of the other nine (#67), but by hand rather than by the pattern: the rows above have just been rewritten to cubic metres, so their names now end in a unit that is no longer theirs and the pattern rightly declines them. With this they are the same name, in the same unit, as BAFU's own `Wood, unspecified, standing/m3` row -- and with the context rules sending all three to `Resource / Biotic`, one resource that arrived as three rows in three compartments and two units is one flow. (#67, #4)

corrections.comment:
8006-14-2 is natural gas's registry number, and gas drawn off a coal seam while the coal is being mined is not natural gas -- it comes out of a mine rather than a gas field, and EF 3.1 says so in words on its `Pit Methane` flow: "Pit methane is a different substance than natural gas (impurities, heating value etc.)". BAFU writes the number on one of its two coal-mine rows, exactly as EF 3.1 writes it on its single copy of the substance and as ecoinvent wrote it on its own until 3.10.1 took it off. The same removal is stated in ef-3.1-manual-fixes.json, ecoinvent-3.8-manual-fixes.json and ecoinvent-3.9.1-manual-fixes.json, so all four lists agree that the number names natural gas and nothing else (#80). It has to come off here too, and taking it off the other three is what makes that urgent: while two flow objects both answered to this number, this row was reported as `multiple-flow-object-candidates` and dropped, which is loud and visible. With one object answering to it, the row would match -- confidently, and onto natural gas.

Matched on the name the row still has when fixes run, `/m3` and all. The general rule that takes a unit back out of a name (#67) runs downstream of this file, not before it, so the m3 row is spelled with its suffix here and only the Nm3 row above has been renamed by hand. The unit is named too, because after that rename `/m3` would otherwise be ambiguous for a reader even though it no longer is for the matcher.

BAFU ships one `Anhydrite` row, a resource in ground measured in kilograms, and gives it no registry number of any kind -- the extracted record has no `cas_numbers` key at all. Anhydrite is anhydrous calcium sulfate, and 7778-18-9 is that substance: Common Chemistry names the number `Calcium sulfate`, ECHA lists it as EC 231-900-3 `Calcium sulfate`, formula Ca.H2O4S, and ecoinvent puts 7778-18-9 on its own `Anhydrite` resource flow in 3.10.1, 3.11 and 3.12. EF 3.1 names the same mineral under the same number: its one resource-from-ground flow for the family carries 7778-18-9 and ships `Anhydrite`, `Natural anhydrite`, `Anhydrous calcium sulfate`, `Karstenite` and `Muriacite` among its synonyms.

Without the number the row has nothing to match on. Measured on a full build of 20 August 2026 at commit df7d1e2, it minted a consensus substance of its own while ecoinvent's anhydrite sat on EF's flow published as `Calcium Sulfate`: one mineral, two lists, two published substances. That is the defect #119 fixes for gypsum, on the other mineral of the pair, and it is the half of it that the EF corrections could not reach -- nothing is wrong with EF here, and nothing is wrong with the mapping. The row simply does not say what it is.

Gypsum stays a separate substance, deliberately. It is the dihydrate, 13397-24-5, a different mineral with a different mass -- 172.172 g/mol against 136.141 -- quarried and traded separately, and #119 gives it a consensus flow of its own that BAFU's and ecoinvent's gypsum rows both reach on that number. Merging the two would need a conversion factor of 0.7907 and would restate a reported gypsum tonnage as a smaller anhydrite one, for a target flow that carries no characterisation factor to offer in exchange. Nothing is converted here: BAFU's row and ecoinvent's are the same mineral in the same unit, so the two join on the number with no rescaling.

`original_value` is `null` rather than `[]`, and the difference matters: the row holds no such key, so the guard reads `None`, and an empty list would be a mismatch -- the fix would warn and decline to apply. Stated rather than omitted so that a future BAFU release shipping a number of its own is not silently overwritten. Matched on the name, which is what this file does throughout because BAFU has no per-flow identifier. One row. (#119)

Arsenic dissolved in water is not just arsenic: it occurs as arsenic III, which is arsenite, and arsenic V, which is arsenate, and the two differ in how mobile and how poisonous they are. `Arsenic V` is arsenate, the arsenic(5+) cation, 17428-41-0, and this list publishes it as `Arsenic(5+)` in fourteen compartments with six characterisation factors in ten of them. BAFU's row carries no registry number, so it minted a second substance -- one flow, no factors, and typed `ImpreciseChemicalMixture`, which is what the list calls something whose composition is not pinned down. A single arsenate ion is not a mixture of anything. The list already publishes this substance and reaches it from every other BAFU row that names it -- cadmium, chromium, lead, manganese, mercury, nickel and zinc all arrive on `basis=cas`, and so does `Chromium III`, which is spelled exactly the way this row is. **Not one BAFU row reaches a charged form on its name.** So where the number is missing, the spelling that would have said which form this is goes unread and the substance is created a second time, with one flow and no characterisation factor beside the one the list already characterises. Giving the row the number is what the other rows already have, and is the same correction #119 made to `Anhydrite`. (#127)

Biogenic carbon dioxide, 124-38-9. BAFU ships this name three times -- `high. pop.`, `low. pop.` and `unspecified` -- and only the `low. pop.` row is missing the number. Without it that row minted `Carbon Dioxide, Biogenic`, a second biogenic carbon dioxide with one flow and no characterisation factor, beside the `Carbon Dioxide (biogenic)` its two siblings reach and EF characterises. BAFU ships 1,532 of its 2,679 rows with no registry number, and 550 of those have a same-named sibling row that does carry one -- the pattern #127 corrected thirty times. It costs nothing on a row whose name alone finds the substance, and it costs the match on a row whose name carries a qualifier: with the number the qualifier narrows the candidates (`cas+qualifier`), and without it the qualified spelling is just an unfamiliar name. Keyed on the name rather than on the row, as every fix in this file is, because BAFU repeats a substance once per subcompartment and a rule keyed on one row goes stale when a subcompartment is added. The siblings that already carry the number are unaffected. (#134)

Read off BAFU's own archive rather than the extracted file: over the 11,948 processes in `BAFU-2026 v1_ecoSpold v1.zip`, 15 of the 398 `high. pop.` exchanges and 5 of the 17 `unspecified` exchanges write 630-08-0, and none of the 117 `low. pop.` exchanges does -- so the number is BAFU's own, written on a minority of exchanges of the two rows that carry it and on none of the third. The siblings that already carry the number are unaffected: a fix that finds its value already in place is a quiet no-op. (#177)

Carbon dioxide in air, filed by BAFU as a biotic resource. BAFU's own flow name says where this carbon comes from -- `in air` -- and its compartment says somewhere else. The list ships the same name in three compartments, `resources / in air`, `resources / biotic` and `resources / unspecified`, and only the first agrees with the name. The other two are the source contradicting itself, which is what a manual fix is for.

It matters because the compartment is published. `resources / unspecified` maps to `Resource → Ground`, so carbon dioxide whose own name says *in air* was published as a resource taken from the ground; `resources / biotic` maps to `Resource → Biotic`, which reads as carbon taken from the biosphere when the carbon is taken *from the atmosphere* and merely ends up in biomass. A resource compartment names where a resource comes from.

Matched on the name **and** the compartment, not on the name alone. Every other fix in this file is keyed on the name because BAFU repeats a substance once per subcompartment and a correction about the substance should reach all of them; this one is a correction about *these two rows*, and the third row of the same name is already right. The pair is the identifying attribute here, and keying on the name alone would rewrite a compartment that needs no rewriting.

With the compartment corrected these rows reach EF's biogenic uptake from air in `Resource → Air`, which is where the curated target in `bafu-2026-v1-match-overrides.json` already sends the substance and where ecoinvent's flow of the same name goes through its own correspondence table (#257). Substance and compartment now agree instead of half-agreeing. (#135)
